dimensions.title: Interface surface
dimensions.rationale: [service] A contract covers its transport: an HTTP contract covers at least 80% of declared routes (generated contracts do), or the application layer over a standard protocol (commands, topics, payloads) is specified in a protocol document or AsyncAPI.
gaps: [service] L4 A second surface: another transport (HTTP and a protocol, two protocols), an MCP server, a CLI with JSON output, or an SDK. (only one programmatic surface)
[cli] L3 Machine-readable output (--json/--format) and documented exit statuses. (no --json/--format option)
[library] L2 The public API is delimited (__all__, an exports map, exported identifiers). (no __all__/exports defining the public API)
dimensions.question: Can another program use it through a documented, machine-readable surface?

requirements.text: A network surface exists: HTTP routes, an MCP server, or a standard protocol listener.

A contract exists: a checked-in OpenAPI/GraphQL/protobuf/AsyncAPI spec, a framework-generated spec, MCP tool schemas, or a standard application protocol that off-the-shelf clients speak (RESP, MQTT, gRPC, PostgreSQL wire, …).

A contract covers its transport: an HTTP contract covers at least 80% of declared routes (generated contracts do), or the application layer over a standard protocol (commands, topics, payloads) is specified in a protocol document or AsyncAPI.
A second surface: another transport (HTTP and a protocol, two protocols), an MCP server, a CLI with JSON output, or an SDK.
Invocable non-interactively: no prompts, or prompts guarded by a TTY check or a --yes/--no-input option.
--help documents every option (at least 90% of options have help text).
Machine-readable output (--json/--format) and documented exit statuses.
The output format is specified by a JSON Schema.
An importable, packaged API exists.
The public API is delimited (__all__, an exports map, exported identifiers).
The public API is statically typed (py.typed, type declarations, a typed language).
An API reference is generated from the code (autodoc, mkdocstrings, typedoc, …).

dimensions.title: Contract stability
dimensions.rationale: Releases are versioned (semver tags or versioned changelog sections).
gaps: L2 A changelog exists and marks breaking changes. (no changelog)
dimensions.question: Can integrators rely on it not changing under them?

requirements.text: Releases are versioned (semver tags or versioned changelog sections).
A changelog exists and marks breaking changes.
A deprecation mechanism is used in code (warnings, @deprecated, Deprecation/Sunset headers) or the API is versioned.
Across tagged releases, no OpenAPI operation, CLI option or __all__ symbol was removed without first being deprecated.

dimensions.title: Events
dimensions.rationale: Webhooks sent by this system, or a streaming endpoint (SSE, WebSocket).
gaps: L3 Signed webhooks registrable through the API, or two mechanisms (webhooks, streams, a broker). (one delivery mechanism, or webhooks that are unsigned or not registrable through the API)
dimensions.question: Can others react to state changes without polling?

requirements.text: Internal events exist (signals, queues, an outbox, emitters).
Webhooks sent by this system, or a streaming endpoint (SSE, WebSocket).
Signed webhooks registrable through the API, or two mechanisms (webhooks, streams, a broker).
requirements.note: one delivery mechanism, or webhooks that are unsigned or not registrable through the API

requirements.text: Events are described by AsyncAPI or CloudEvents.

dimensions.title: Identity
gaps: L4 Standard provisioning or federation (OIDC client credentials, SCIM). (no OIDC client credentials or SCIM)
dimensions.question: Can a machine act with its own revocable, least-privilege identity?

requirements.text: Programmatic authentication (bearer tokens, API keys).
Per-client, revocable credentials (managed API keys, service accounts) or OAuth2.
Credentials carry scopes or permissions.
Standard provisioning or federation (OIDC client credentials, SCIM).
requirements.note: no OIDC client credentials or SCIM

dimensions.title: Data portability
dimensions.rationale: Not applicable: owns no persistent data.
dimensions.question: Can its data get in and out, in bulk, in open formats, with an explicit schema?

dimensions.title: Agent ergonomics
dimensions.rationale: [service] Field-level validation errors, and paginated lists.
gaps: [service] L3 Typed errors (RFC 9457 over HTTP, or a standard protocol's typed error codes), idempotent writes (Idempotency-Key), and rate-limit signals. (no typed errors)
[cli] L3 Documented exit statuses distinguish error classes, errors are JSON in JSON mode, and color is off when not a TTY. (exit statuses aren't documented)
[library] L1 Errors are specific exception types, and library code never calls sys.exit. (library code exits the process: scripts/add_latest_release_date.py, scripts/notify_translations.py)
dimensions.question: Can an automated caller use it without guessing, and recover from failure?

requirements.text: Errors are machine-readable: consistent JSON over HTTP, or a standard protocol's native error replies (RESP errors, MQTT reason codes, gRPC status, SQLSTATE).
Field-level validation errors, and paginated lists.
Typed errors (RFC 9457 over HTTP, or a standard protocol's typed error codes), idempotent writes (Idempotency-Key), and rate-limit signals.
Dry-run or validate-only, conditional requests, and agent docs.
Never blocks on a prompt when stdin is not a TTY.
Data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, non-zero exit on failure.
Documented exit statuses distinguish error classes, errors are JSON in JSON mode, and color is off when not a TTY.
--dry-run, limits for long or costly operations (timeouts, budgets), and agent docs.
Errors are specific exception types, and library code never calls sys.exit.
requirements.note: library code exits the process: scripts/add_latest_release_date.py, scripts/notify_translations.py

requirements.text: Inputs are validated with messages naming the bad argument.
Timeouts and retries are configurable.
Agent docs, and examples that run as tests (doctests).

dimensions.title: Embeddability

[cli] L3 Published to a public registry and run non-interactively in CI. (the command isn't run in CI)

dimensions.title: Extensibility
dimensions.rationale: Not yet: Internal seams: a registry, registration function or plugin manager.
gaps: L1 Internal seams: a registry, registration function or plugin manager. (no registry or registration function)

requirements.text: Internal seams: a registry, registration function or plugin manager.

Out-of-tree extensions are discovered (entry points, a plugin directory, configuration) without editing the package.

dimensions.title: Observability
dimensions.rationale: [cli] Meaningful exit statuses, and errors on stderr.
gaps: [service] L1 A health or readiness endpoint, or a container healthcheck. (no health endpoint or healthcheck)
